en: When Mayon Volcano erupts, wearing an N95 mask protects your lungs from harmful volcanic ash.
Living near Tacloban City's coast means you must evacuate inland during a typhoon to avoid deadly storm surges.
Wading in floodwaters around Manila after heavy rain can expose you to leptospirosis bacteria from rat urine.
If a strong earthquake strikes while you are in Davao Oriental, immediately move to higher ground to avoid tsunamis.
During the rainy season in Quezon Province, emptying stagnant water in tires prevents mosquitoes from breeding and spreading dengue.
In May, the extreme heat index in Tuguegarao City, Cagayan requires you to drink extra water to avoid heatstroke.
During heavy monsoon rains, residents in the mountainous province of Ifugao must watch out for dangerous landslides along steep slopes.
While snorkeling in the Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park, wearing reef-safe sunscreen prevents harmful chemicals from damaging the coral.
Because the West Valley Fault runs through Metro Manila, your family should secure heavy cabinets to the walls.
Swimming in Laguna de Bay during algal blooms can cause skin rashes, so always check local water quality advisories.
When exploring the Puerto Princesa Subterranean River, wearing a mask protects your lungs from inhaling harmful bat guano dust.
If you are camping near the Cagayan River, never set up your tent on the dry riverbed during rainy weather.
